author: reek
body: The [Device] shader form of the bare-metal fireworks simulation. One GPU thread owns one spark. Each thread derives its spark's launch angle and speed from its global index, integrates the ballistic arc under gravity for the current frame, fades the color over the spark's life, and writes the packed pixel back to a global output buffer. Compiled through the PTX and SPIR-V plugs, the [Device]-effected kernels below become real GPU shader code -- the same physics the CPU preview runs, now per-thread.

author: reek
body: fw-burst-spark: procedural burst. The spark index gives its ray angle and a jittered speed; the thread integrates x/y under gravity, fades the brightness over life, and packs (brightness, x, y) into one word stored at out[gid]. The trig is pure; the single global write is the tail.

author: reek
body: fw-integrate: read-modify-write. Each thread loads its spark's four packed state words (x, y, vx, vy) from the state buffer, advances one frame of ballistic motion, and stores the new screen position to out. The four global reads are act-bound; the store is the tail.
